name: MN-06
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+10 district and a long-serving, well-funded incumbent give Emmer a strong structural edge
Chapin's $439K raised and $70K on hand are dwarfed by Emmer's $4.5M war chest
No public polls or expert ratings; prediction markets put Democratic odds near one in ten
A Democratic-tilted national environment is the main force narrowing the expected margin
model.rationale: Emmer pairs a ten-point Republican district lean with a dominant fundraising position, while Chapin has raised little money and drawn no outside spending. With no public polling, prediction markets and fundamentals both point to a comfortable Republican hold, though not quite a safe one.
model.watch: A decisive national Democratic wave or an unexpected surge in the challenger's visibility and funding could pull the margin into single digits.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Minnesota's sixth district leans ten points Republican, and incumbent Tom Emmer has held the seat through several elections. He enters 2026 with a large financial edge, having raised nearly $9.8 million and holding $4.5 million on hand. Democrat Doug Chapin has raised about $439,000 with limited cash remaining, and a third-party candidate also appears on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give Democrats roughly a one-in-ten chance of an upset. The district's Republican lean, Emmer's incumbency, and his fundraising dominance point to a comfortable Republican hold, though a strongly favorable national environment for Democrats could narrow the margin somewhat.
